connection_type: I have direct personal experience (as an immigrant, refugee, religious minority, or member of a marginalised group)
disclosure_text: I have been an immigrant in Canada with my family for last 8 years and I am a part of Hindu religion, which is a religious minority. I am brown in color, which is again a minority in this country.
micronarrative: I identify as a member of a religious minority group, and the scenario resonates because we often cannot celebrate our culture or religion freely without fear. There is always resistance from people, forcing individuals to follow the majority. I remember a specific religious day where my spouse had to see the moon to break their fast; people around the neighborhood were literally staring at us. This visibility translates into tangible economic consequences. As a religious minority, people often do not offer jobs and do not support our businesses. Because of this economic vulnerability, I believe the bakery owner should not have posted the picture. The risk of facing hostility and financial pressure is too high when the community is already predisposed against us.
